get.description:
Retrieve an asset by its full unified slug.

Unified asset slugs look like ``{workspace-slug}/catalog/{entity-slug}``
(e.g. ``the-robot-studio/catalog/so101``). They contain slashes and
therefore can't round-trip through the single-segment
``/assets/{uuid}`` route even when URL-encoded — the FE was falling
back to a registry-id list query that mis-matched whenever the slug
wasn't also the registry id (registry ids don't include the
``/catalog/`` segment).

Mirrors the by-slug pattern already used by
``/environments/by-slug``, ``/twins/by-slug`` and
``/mlmodels/by-slug`` so the FE has one consistent way to resolve
whatever slug the user just typed into the address bar.

Registered early in the router (before any ``/{uuid}``-shaped
routes) so Django-Ninja's registration-ordered matcher doesn't let
the greedy ``/{uuid}`` route swallow ``/by-slug`` first.

Anonymous-friendly: public assets resolve without auth; authenticated
callers additionally see private assets they have access to. When
the caller can't read a private match we return 404 (not 403) to
avoid leaking existence.

List public catalog assets that have a registry_id_alias (shortcut) set.

These are the "primitive" assets — curated catalog entries with a short
alias such as ``camera`` or ``lidar`` that can be instantiated directly
by alias, making it easy to populate an environment programmatically.

Get the most popular tags from asset metadata.
Results are cached for 1 hour for performance.

Check if a registry_id is available for use.

Returns:
    - available: True if the registry_id is not in use
    - registry_id: The normalized registry_id
    - suggestion: If not available, suggests an alternative

Resolve an asset by ``registry_id``/alias passed as a query parameter.

Vendor-scoped registry_ids contain a slash (``vendor/slug``). Encoding that
slash into a path segment (``%2F``) is unreliable because proxies in front
of the backend normalize ``%2F`` back to ``/`` before routing, so the
single-segment path route 404s. Taking the identifier as a query parameter
sidesteps that entirely, which is what the catalog sync relies on to look up
and evict (soft-deleted) squatters via the slash-free ``/{uuid}`` routes.

Always responds ``200`` with ``{"found": bool, ...}`` (never ``404`` for a
missing asset) so callers can distinguish "asset not found" from "this
endpoint isn't deployed" (a real ``404``) and fail closed accordingly.

``include_deleted=true`` also matches soft-deleted rows and is restricted to
staff/admin to avoid leaking deleted asset existence.

Get the list of vendors that have public assets.
Used by frontend to whitelist vendor pages for unauthenticated access.
Results are cached for 1 hour for performance.

Import an asset from a .cbw package file.

The .cbw package should be a zip file created by the export endpoint,
containing manifest.json, asset.json, and associated files.

This allows transferring assets between Cyberwave instances.

Requires an active membership of the target workspace.

Parameters:
    file: The .cbw file to import
    workspace_uuid: Optional target workspace UUID. If not provided, uses user's first workspace.
    custom_registry_id: Optional custom registry ID for the imported asset.
        If not provided, uses the original registry_id from the package.

This is useful for processing workflows where an uploaded attachment
gets converted/processed into the main GLB visualization file.

Import a LAS, LAZ, or raw PLY scan as a correctly-sized splat PLY.

A PLY that turns out to hold Gaussian data is preserved as a splat instead of

Upload a Gaussian splatting file (.ply/.splat/.spz/.ksplat) as the asset's

post.description:
Expand an adapter action into a canonical :class:`MotionEpisodeSchema`.

ADR 0001 P3. Single entry point for every ``ActionAdapter`` on the
client (``graspToEpisode``, ``pointTrajectoryToEpisode`` when it
wants a metric solve, ``eeDeltaToEpisode`` for VLA replay). The
browser stays free of IK; the edge worker can mirror the same
contract later for low-latency / offline runs.

The current MVP returns an **EE-only** episode — joint positions
are left empty and ``ee_positions`` carries the world-space path.
That's enough to drive the existing :class:`TrajectoryPlayer`
EE-only renderer on the frontend (P2). A joint-level IK solver
(pinocchio, per the ADR open decision) will be dropped in behind
this function without changing the endpoint signature or the
schema.

We look the asset up to validate authorization — even though the
first-cut expansion ignores the URDF, we keep the endpoint scoped
to an asset so the solver upgrade later can read the URDF directly
without needing a migration of any caller.

Generate a response using a Vision Language Model (VLM) with the given prompt and image.

This endpoint uses Google's Gemini 3 Pro vision model to analyze images and generate
text responses based on the provided prompt.

Args:

    uuid: The asset UUID (currently unused but kept for API consistency)
    payload: Contains the prompt and image_url to analyze

Returns:

patch.description:
Update the asset's universal schema using JSON Pointer operations.

This allows editing the asset schema, including:
- /sensors (array of sensor objects)
- /extensions/cyberwave/capabilities
- /links, /joints, /actuators, etc.

When capabilities are patched, they are validated using CapabilitiesValidator.

Body:
    {
        "op": "add" | "replace",
        "path": "/sensors/0/parameters/id",
        "value": "my_camera"
    }

Returns:
    {"schema": <updated schema>, "updated": {"op": "...", "path": "..."}}

If the operation moved a joint's zero (`/joints/N/pose` or `/joints/N/axis`)
the response also carries `zero_moved_joints` and a `warning` — see
:func:`_zero_moved_response_fields`.

get.description:
Get the asset's universal schema as JSON (for download).
Supports both authenticated and anonymous access (for public assets).

patch.description:
Apply an RFC 7386 JSON Merge Patch to exactly one named sensor, leaving every
sibling sensor and every omitted field untouched. Add, delete, and rename are
out of scope (400) and must go through the batch ``PATCH /universal-schema``
endpoint instead.

Apply many JSON Pointer operations to the asset's universal schema at once.

Operations are applied in order, so each one observes the result of the
previous ones — identical to issuing the same operations as sequential
single-op PATCH requests, but the schema hash, the database write and the
stored-URDF regeneration are each performed once for the whole batch instead
of once per operation.

All-or-nothing: if any operation fails, nothing is persisted and the 400 body
identifies the offending operation by index, op and path (never its value,
which can be large).

Body:
    {
        "operations": [
            {"op": "replace", "path": "/joints/0/type", "value": "continuous"},
            {"op": "add", "path": "/sensors", "value": [...]}
        ]
    }

Returns:
    {"schema": <updated schema>, "applied": <int>, "changed": <bool>}

``changed`` is false when the operations reproduced the stored schema, in
which case no write and no regeneration were performed.

If the batch moved a joint's zero (`/joints/N/pose` or `/joints/N/axis`) the
response also carries `zero_moved_joints` and a `warning` — see
:func:`_zero_moved_response_fields`.

post.description:
Trigger regeneration of an Asset's universal_schema from its URDFProject.

By default, queues a Celery task and returns immediately. Pass `?sync=true`
to execute synchronously and block until complete (useful for local testing).

The rebuild re-parses the stored URDF, which cannot express every schema
field. By default everything authored outside the URDF is carried forward:
per-joint `home_position`, `/sensors`, `/actuators`,
`/extensions/cyberwave/capabilities` and `/collision_config`. Pass
`?preserve_authored=false` to discard it and take the parse wholesale — the
right choice when the URDF itself genuinely changed.

Returns:
    {
        "queued": bool,
        "asset_uuid": "...",
        "urdf_project_uuid": "...",
        "preserve_authored": bool,
    }

Return workflow and node execution events bounded to a replay window.

``limit`` caps the events returned (default 500, max 2000).

``order`` picks which end of the window survives that cap as well as the
order the response reads in: a live view polling "now - 24h ... now"
wants the most recent events, and ``asc`` would hand it the start of
yesterday and drop everything since. ``desc`` answers newest-first, the
same way it does on twin telemetry.

``include_payloads=False`` drops each node execution's ``input_data`` and
``output_data``. They are unbounded — a full page of them runs to several
megabytes, most of it ``output_data`` — so a view that polls this endpoint
and only renders titles and timestamps should not be paying to serialise
them every few seconds.

patch.description: Merge editor hierarchy keys without replacing unrelated settings.

Set the environment's georeference (where on Earth its origin sits).

Unlike ``patch_environment_navigation_settings`` this is an all-or-nothing
write: the whole ``geo`` dict is replaced, and the server owns
``contract_version`` / ``source`` / ``anchor_status`` / ``set_at`` / ``set_by``
so a client cannot forge a "manual" status onto an unverified anchor.

A dedicated endpoint rather than ``PUT /{uuid}`` because that path replaces
``settings`` wholesale, and ``settings`` is also home to ``navigation``,
``twin_order`` and ``scene_order`` -- a geo save through it can silently revert
a concurrent scene reorder or the mapping bridge's anchor status.

delete.description:
Remove the environment's georeference.

Refuses while GPS-positioned twins depend on it: deleting the anchor out from
under a live twin would leave it with nothing to convert its fixes against,
which is exactly the silent breakage this feature exists to avoid.

get.description:
List every AprilTag/ArUco marker in the environment with its ground-truth.

Intended for perception/detection harnesses: returns each marker's family,
id, physical size, and true world pose so detected markers can be scored
against the truth without parsing the compiled primitive blob.

Return the marker's black/white pattern PNG.

The same deterministic raster bound into the MuJoCo scene, so the 3D editor
and 2D preview render the exact pattern a simulated camera sees.

post.description:
Rasterize this environment's geometry into a navigable occupancy grid.

The counterpart to SLAM: the result is an ordinary ``MapData`` occupancy
grid, so the viewer overlay and the edge's preloaded-map path consume it
unchanged. Write access, because it also binds the environment's navigation
anchor to the map it produces.

get.description:
The same raster, rendered to PNG and not stored.

This is what makes the traversability band tunable: an operator drops the
step-over height, sees the floor rails reappear, and only then commits. Read
access is enough because nothing is written.

PNG rather than the stored PGM so a browser can display it directly; the
pixel values are identical.

post.description:
The current poses of a Move Twin node's waypoints.

A compiled edge worker calls this when the node runs, so a waypoint moved
since compilation (e.g. by Move Waypoint earlier in the same run) is driven
to where it is now. Resolved exactly as the compiler resolves the poses it
bakes in -- see ``src.lib.move_twin_waypoint_poses``.

get.description:
Whether a workflow run is currently walking this environment.

Exists so the client can disable waypoint authoring and NAME the blocking
run, using the same query that ``_require_no_active_run`` enforces with —
a client that derived this independently would eventually disagree with the
server about whether the route is locked.

Preferred over fanning out ``useEnvironmentWorkflowExecutions`` (one request
per workflow, polled) purely to answer a boolean.

patch.description:
Update a single waypoint's stored position/rotation offset.

Deliberately narrower than the bulk replace path: only ``position``/
``rotation`` can be changed here, never ``frame`` — re-anchoring what
a waypoint is relative to is an authoring-time decision made in the
environment editor, not a workflow action (see ``move_waypoint``
workflow node).

post.description:
Save a browser-captured screenshot as the environment's thumbnail.

The frontend's environment viewer snapshots its WebGL canvas (JPEG, see
``environment-thumbnail-capture-handler.tsx``) on a dwell timer while the
env is open, and posts the bytes here. This bypasses the Celery + headless
screenshot path for any env the user has actually opened — cheaper, faster,
and the resulting image reflects the framing the user chose rather than a
default isometric view. Accepts both ``image/jpeg`` and ``image/png``;
bytes are stored as-is with no re-encoding.

get.description:
Get twins in an environment with optional dynamic filters.

Supports filtering on any field using query parameters with Django lookup syntax.

Examples:
- GET /environments/{uuid}/twins?position_x__gte=0&position_x__lte=10
- GET /environments/{uuid}/twins?capabilities__locomotion_mode=wheeled
- GET /environments/{uuid}/twins?metadata__power__battery_percent__gte=20
- GET /environments/{uuid}/twins?metadata__amr__navigation__status=idle
- GET /environments/{uuid}/twins?asset__uuid=xxx
- GET /environments/{uuid}/twins?capabilities__amr__vehicle_type=forklift

Get persisted driver logs across an environment's twins, newest-first.

This is the read path for any view that shows more than one twin's logs —
the workbench Logs tab and the replay log panel. It exists as an
environment route rather than as a twin-set filter on
``GET /twins/{uuid}/logs`` for one concrete reason: a twin set in the query
string grows with twin count (~37 bytes per UUID), so a large environment
would push the request line past the 4–8 KB limit common on proxies and
start failing outright. One environment UUID does not.

``TwinDriverLog`` has no environment column (see its docstring: driver logs
are "always queried twin-first", and every composite index is
``twin_uuid``-prefixed), so the environment is resolved to its live twins
and the predicate is still ``twin_uuid IN (...)``. The environment scope
lives in the URL and the ACL, not in the SQL. Rows carry ``twin_uuid``
because they are interleaved.

Query params:
- twin_uuids: comma-separated UUIDs to narrow to, all of which must be
  twins of this environment. Omit for every twin in it.
- limit: max rows to return (default 100, max 10000)
- offset: number of rows to skip (default 0)
- level: optional severity filter (case-insensitive, exact match)
- start: optional inclusive start datetime (ISO format)
- end: optional inclusive end datetime (ISO format)
- include_total: when false, skip the ``COUNT`` and serve ``total: null``

Access is one check on the environment. Since a twin's role is the greater
of its own and its environment's (see ``Twin.highest_role_for``), reading
the environment already clears every twin in it, so narrowing can only
shrink an authorized set and never widen it.

get.description:
List a stable, filterable recording catalog.

Every response is a bounded, newest-first page ordered by
``(effective_start_us, uuid)`` descending. With no date filters it covers
the environment's whole eligible history, not only its latest day. Omitting
``limit`` returns the first ``CATALOG_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`` (100) items; a
supplied ``limit`` above ``CATALOG_MAX_PAGE_SIZE`` (max 100) is a 422, not a
clamped page. Follow ``next_cursor`` while ``has_more`` is true to read the
selected catalog.

A date window is applied only when both ``start_date`` and ``end_date``
(or both legacy ``start_timestamp``/``end_timestamp`` aliases) are given.
``include_unready=false`` always returns ready rows only;
``include_unready=true`` is restricted to staff/administrators. When it is
omitted, non-administrators receive ready rows only and staff/admin users
follow the deployment's ``RECORDINGS_READY_ONLY_DEFAULT`` policy. Repeated
twin/context/source filters are ORed within a kind and ANDed across kinds.

``active_only=true`` narrows to recordings still being written. Use it to
watch for an in-progress recording instead of polling the newest page: the
catalog is ordered by start time, so a long-running recording with enough
newer ones ahead of it is not on page 1, and a newest-page poll would stop
seeing it while it is still being written.

Return recording-date availability without media IO.

With no date or catalog filters this covers every eligible recording in the
environment; unlike the catalog endpoint it is never paginated. ``timezone``
defaults to ``UTC`` and controls the date buckets and first/last dates.
Date-window and ``include_unready`` defaults/authorization are identical to
:func:`get_environment_recordings`: give both date bounds to filter, pass
``include_unready=false`` for ready rows only, and do not rely on an omitted
readiness flag when a predictable staff/admin result is required.

Return one keyset page of window annotations for a set of time ranges.

This resolves no recording. The caller already holds every window it wants
annotated (catalog descriptors carry their own start/end), so requiring a
recording here only bought a lookup against the largest table we have —
once per recording, to re-derive timestamps the caller passed in anyway.

``windows`` is ``start_us:end_us`` pairs, comma separated. Overlapping and
touching ranges are merged, so selecting forty back-to-back recordings costs
one or two range predicates rather than forty. Ordering is ascending by
``(timestamp_us, kind, uuid)`` and paging is keyset: unlike a newest-first
``LIMIT``, the oldest windows in a sparse multi-day selection cannot be
starved of annotations by a denser recent one. One page carries at most 2000
annotations (``limit`` default 500).

Events come back with no recording association. Mapping an annotation to the
recordings whose window contains it — and applying any per-recording context
policy — belongs to the caller, which is the only side that knows each
window's recording identity and context.

Return signed URLs and minimal metadata for replay (no sampled frames).

Deliberately narrow instead of going through ``PUT /twins/{uuid}`` with a
``metadata`` blob: that call merges metadata only at the TOP level, so a
client sending its own ``status`` block replaces the whole sub-dict — and the
copy a client holds is the one it fetched, wiping whatever the edge has
written to ``metadata.status`` since, including ``is_flying``, the
aircraft-reported value the redundant-takeoff guard depends on. Here the client sends only the
intent it owns and the server merges it, so operator intent and aircraft
truth can be written concurrently by their respective owners.

The merge is done on a re-read under a row lock rather than on the copy the
ACL decorator fetched. ``metadata`` is a single JSON column replaced whole on
save, and the edge writes ``status.is_flying`` into it from
``MQTTClient.update_twin_flight_state`` at 0.5 Hz per drone — so a report
landing between that fetch and this save would be overwritten by a
read-modify-write, which is the very clobber this endpoint exists to avoid.

authored ``position_x/y/z``; GPS is not produced by any simulation backend.

Two things are validated up front so a misconfiguration surfaces here rather
than mid-flight, when the only symptom would be a drone that will not appear:

1. The environment must already carry a valid geo anchor. Without one there is
   nothing to convert a fix against.
2. The twin (or its asset) must declare a ``gps`` sensor in its universal
   schema. The structural fact "this robot has a GNSS receiver" belongs there;
   this endpoint only records the *routing* decision that the receiver drives
   the rendered pose.

Deliberately narrow rather than ``PUT /twins/{uuid}`` with a ``metadata`` blob,
for the same reason as ``set_twin_flight_request`` above: that path merges
metadata only at the top level, so a client sending a stale copy would wipe
whatever the edge has written to ``metadata.status`` since it fetched. The
merge here happens on a re-read under a row lock, and touches only the ``gps``
key.

``schema_hash`` describes the whole schema this response was built from, not
the (possibly scoped) ``value``. Round-trip it as ``expected_schema_hash`` on
the next PATCH.

It is returned here, rather than being read off ``TwinSchema.schema_hash``,
because that field arrives on a *different* request: an editor pairing a
document from this endpoint with a hash from an older twins query holds a token
that vouches for a schema it never saw. One read has to yield both.

patch.description:
Update the twin's universal schema using JSON Pointer operations.

This allows editing twin-specific schema overrides, such as:
- /sensors (array of sensor objects)
- /extensions/cyberwave/capabilities

Note: Unlike Asset schema, Twin schema PATCH does NOT update a hash
(twin schema is a snapshot, not authoritative).

Body:
    {
        "op": "add" | "replace",
        "path": "/sensors/0/parameters/id",
        "value": "my_camera"
    }

Returns:
    {"schema": <updated schema>, "updated": {"op": "...", "path": "..."}}

Apply many JSON Pointer operations to the twin's universal schema at once.

Operations are applied in order, so each one observes the result of the
previous ones — identical to issuing them as sequential single-op PATCH
requests, but the deep copy, the schema validation, the database write and the
MQTT notification are each performed once for the whole batch instead of once
per operation.

Schema validation runs on the final schema rather than after every operation.
Since the batch is all-or-nothing, only that final state is ever persisted.

All-or-nothing: if any operation fails, nothing is persisted and the 400 body
identifies the offending operation by index, op and path (never its value).

Body:
    {
        "operations": [
            {"op": "add", "path": "/sensors", "value": [...]},
            {"op": "replace", "path": "/sensors/0/parameters/id", "value": "cam"}
        ]
    }

Returns:
    {"schema": <updated schema>, "applied": <int>, "changed": <bool>}

stream. Filters to:

    cannot legally reference this twin's cameras and loading
    them would be an avoidable cross-tenant scan.
  - Active workflows (``is_active=True``) only — inactive
    workflows aren't running, so their zones aren't armed.
  - Non-disabled, non-deleted nodes (including intermediates;
    a disabled ``call_model`` in the middle of the chain
    means the runtime won't reach the spatial_filter, so the
    zone shouldn't render).
  - Zones whose chain is rooted in a ``camera_frame`` trigger
    bound to this twin (the chain may go through arbitrary
    ``call_model`` / ``annotate`` / ``anonymize`` filters first
    — same upstream-traversal contract the editor uses).

    workspace membership is the usual source of that permission,
    but ``ObjectRoleAssignment`` can downgrade it for specific

The traversal runs against an in-memory adjacency map built
from a single ``WorkflowConnection`` query so chain depth costs

- frame_bucket: ``"policy_depth"`` to fetch the policy-resolution depth

The ``audio_format`` query parameter selects the output codec:

- **mp3** (default) — returns the pre-built MP3 created when the

- **ogg** — lossless concat of the original Opus OGG chunks into a

The endpoint also:

- Creates an ``edge_core_restart`` lifecycle alert (when an
  environment can be resolved) so all viewers of the environment
  see the deliberate restart, not just the requester.  Edge-core
  transitions this alert through ``in_progress`` → ``completed`` /

  marks it ``timed_out`` when the command never lands.
- Pre-resolves any active "restart-fixable" alerts on the bound
  twins (see ``EDGE_CORE_RESTART_RESOLVABLE_ALERT_TYPES``) so the
  workbench is not cluttered with stale failure noise while the
  restart proceeds.  Each resolved alert is annotated with the
  originating ``request_id`` so the audit trail is preserved.

1. Create lifecycle alert (best-effort)
2. Publish MQTT command (fatal if it fails — we never want to
   resolve prior alerts without the restart actually being queued)
3. Pre-resolve policy alerts (best-effort)
4. Annotate lifecycle alert with the list of pre-resolved UUIDs

- 200 + populated ``request_ids`` — at least one publish queued.
- 200 + ``skipped_reason`` and empty body — declarative no-op

  partial broker failure; the queued subset still succeeded.

  least one twin and every attempt raised. Matches
  ``POST /twins/{uuid}/sync-workflows``'s "raise on broker error"
  behaviour so retry/backoff logic can branch on status code.

post.description:
Regenerate a joint keyboard controller's bindings from its linked asset's
**current** ``universal_schema``.

Staff-only maintenance action for re-deriving a controller whose bindings no
longer match the asset schema they were seeded from. It reuses the exact
generator the seed pipeline uses (``generate_joint_controller_from_asset``),
so the result matches what a fresh seed of this asset would produce.

Unlike ``POST /catalog/seed-autogen-controllers`` (which regenerates the
autogen catalog from *production* assets), this reads only this backend's
stored schema, so it fixes dev without depending on prod being patched first.

Pass ``asset_uuid`` to disambiguate when the policy links more than one asset.

**What happens to the existing controller.** It is rewritten **in place** —
same row, same ``uuid``/slug/name/``controller_type``/linked assets, so every
twin attachment, policy link, and saved reference keeps working and nothing
is duplicated. Only ``metadata`` is written (``update_fields=["metadata"]``).

Within ``metadata``, the keys the generator emits (``keyboard_bindings``,
``control_mode``, ``input_device``, ``multiple_joints_update``,
``show_keyboard_visualizer``) are **overwritten** with freshly derived
values; ``keyboard_bindings`` is replaced wholesale, not merged per binding.
So any hand-edited key assignment on this controller is lost — that is the
point of the action, but there is no undo and no snapshot of the previous
bindings. Every other stored key is preserved, and the catalog-seed identity
key is explicitly carried over so the row stays recognizable as its catalog
entry. Other controllers, including other ones for the same asset, are not
touched: this acts only on the policy in the URL.

Regeneration is idempotent — calling it again with an unchanged schema
produces the same bindings — and it refuses to write (400) when the asset
schema yields no controllable joints, rather than clearing the bindings.

get.description:
Request a download URL for a dataset in a specific format.

This endpoint is **idempotent**: calling it multiple times will not spawn
duplicate conversion tasks.

Because it is both the initiate and the poll endpoint, a *failed* conversion
reports itself as 409 ``conversion_failed`` rather than being replaced with a
fresh attempt — otherwise a client polling every few seconds spawns a new
conversion task on every tick and never learns that it failed. Pass
``retry=true`` to explicitly start a new attempt.

Supported ``format`` values (``DatasetType`` values)
----------------------------------------------------
- ``parquet``   — Cyberwave joined-parquet zip (native datasets only).
                  Deprecated alias: ``plain``.
- ``lerobot3``  — LeRobot v3 (Forge writer).
                  Deprecated alias: ``lerobot``.
- ``lerobot21`` — LeRobot v2.1 (Forge writer).
- ``rlds``      — RLDS / TF-Record (Open-X-Embodiment style, Forge writer).
- ``openvla``   — Cyberwave OpenVLA TFDS bundle (Cyberwave-generated writer).
- ``robodm``    — Berkeley .vla format (Forge writer).

Planned / not yet implemented (returns 422):
``mcap``, ``gr00t``, ``hdf5``, ``zarr``, ``rosbag``

Returns
-------
HTTP 200 (``DatasetDownloadReadySchema``)
    The artifact is ready; ``signed_url`` is valid for 24 h.
HTTP 202 (``DatasetDownloadProcessingSchema``)
    A conversion task was queued or is already running.
    Poll ``poll_url`` (this endpoint) again until you get a 200.
HTTP 409
    The dataset cannot be converted (``dataset_not_convertible``), or the
    last attempt for this format failed (``conversion_failed``).
HTTP 422
    The format is not supported (either invalid or TODO).

TwinGpsSettingsPatchSchema.description:
Whether and how a twin's live position is derived from its GNSS fixes.

LIVE MODE ONLY -- GPS is not produced by any simulation backend, so in
Simulate the twin renders from its authored pose instead.

Every field is required when enabling, and none has a server-side default,
because each one changes where the twin is drawn: a rover whose
``vertical_source`` silently defaulted to ``gps_altitude`` would hover or sink
by the GNSS vertical error, and a ``max_horizontal_accuracy_m`` nobody chose is
a threshold nobody can be held to.

``position_source: "static"`` needs no other field -- it removes the whole
configuration rather than storing the string, so there is one representation
of one state.

position_source.description: 'gps' derives live position from GNSS fixes; 'static' clears the configuration and returns the twin to its authored pose
position_source.title: Position Source

yaw_source.description: Required when enabling. 'compass_heading' turns the twin to the fix's true-north heading; 'none' leaves yaw to the twin's rotation stream
yaw_source.title: Yaw Source

vertical_source.description: Required when enabling. 'gps_altitude' takes Z from the fix; 'anchor_plane' pins Z to the geo anchor's plane (ground robots, 2D fixes)
vertical_source.title: Vertical Source

min_fix_quality.description: Required when enabling. Weakest fix type accepted. Publishers that omit fix_type entirely (e.g. the DJI node) are accepted with unverified quality.
min_fix_quality.title: Min Fix Quality

max_horizontal_accuracy_m.description: Required when enabling. Fixes reporting worse horizontal accuracy than this are rejected. Publishers that omit the field are accepted.
max_horizontal_accuracy_m.title: Max Horizontal Accuracy M

TwinGpsSettingsPatchSchema.title: TwinGpsSettingsPatchSchema

``pre_resolved_alert_uuids`` lists any prior runtime-failure alerts
(see ``EDGE_CORE_RESTART_RESOLVABLE_ALERT_TYPES``) that this
restart auto-resolved on the edge's bound twins.  Empty when no

directly so it can say "Restart requested. Cleared N prior failure

JointStatesSchema.description:
ROS-style ``sensor_msgs/JointState`` projection.

``velocity`` / ``effort`` arrays follow ROS semantics: an empty array
means the channel is not measured/commanded for any joint. They are
only populated when every reported joint carries an explicit value.

``position_source`` is a Cyberwave extension parallel to ``name``, and the
only way a caller can tell a measured pose from a fabricated one. Every
controllable joint is reported, and a joint with no recorded runtime state
falls back to its authored ``home_position`` and then to the geometric zero
— which on the wire is indistinguishable from a robot that really is at
home or at zero. A client that treats a ``home``/``default`` row as a live
reading will show a never-moved joint as measured, and (in teleop) will step
from a pose nothing ever observed. ``state`` identifies persisted runtime
state, not its freshness. ``source=simulation`` requires a fresh observation
from the active simulation and returns its timestamp/session metadata;
it never falls back to the saved scene pose.
JointStatesSchema.title: JointStatesSchema

``autogenerated_source`` is always the current compiler output (or

in pixels and ``cx``, ``cy`` is the principal point in pixels. Distortion
is intentionally out of scope for v1; callers that need it can pass it
through :attr:`MLModelRunSchema.params` until the field stabilises.

``width`` and ``height`` accept whole-number floats (e.g. ``640.0``) and
coerce them to ``int`` so callers that forward raw JSON from camera drivers
don't need to cast on their side.

optional name of the reference frame (e.g. ``"world"``, ``"base_link"``)
so a multi-camera request can mix wrist-relative and world-relative
poses without the runner having to guess.

MLModelFrameSchema.description:

Used by perception tasks that need a temporal or multi-camera context
(e.g. ``detect_relations`` across a short clip, wrist + overhead views).
At least one of ``image_base64`` / ``image_url`` must be set.

``timestamp`` is an optional monotonic millisecond offset from the first
frame and ``camera_id`` is an optional free-form label (e.g. ``"wrist"``
/ ``"overhead"``) so downstream runners can align frames from multiple
cameras. Both are advisory — the ordering in ``frames`` is authoritative.
MLModelFrameSchema.title: MLModelFrameSchema

RobotContextSchema.description:

Kept separate from :class:`RobotStateSchema` because it changes
rarely (maybe per-run) whereas ``robot_state`` changes per-frame.
``frame_id`` is the reference frame that the request's poses /
intrinsics are expressed in — typically ``"base_link"`` for
robot-mounted cameras, ``"world"`` for fixed cameras. Callers that
omit it fall back to the provider's default assumption.
RobotContextSchema.title: RobotContextSchema

RobotStateSchema.description:
Current state of a robot at the moment of capture.

ADR 0001 P5. Optional envelope field on :class:`MLModelRunSchema`.
Populated by the caller when known (e.g. the twin page has it
already, or the edge worker snapshotted it at the same timestamp
as the frame). When ``twin_uuid`` is set and ``robot_state`` is
omitted, the backend auto-pulls the twin's latest state — explicit
``robot_state`` in the request always wins.

Fields are intentionally loose: not every robot exposes all of
them, and not every VLA / IK consumer needs all of them. A runner
that wants "just the joint vector" reads ``joint_positions``; a
runner that wants EE pose reads ``ee_pose``; a runner that wants
both (rare) reads both.
RobotStateSchema.title: RobotStateSchema

MLModelRunSchema.description:
Payload for the interactive playground run endpoint.

Primary contract (backwards-compatible): at least one of ``prompt``,
``image_base64``, or ``image_url`` must be provided. ``structured_task``
is an optional hint for building a provider-specific prompt (e.g.
``detect_points`` for Gemini Robotics ER which returns ``[y, x]`` points
normalized to 0-1000).

Extended perception envelope (all optional, additive):

* ``frames`` — ordered list of image frames. When set, ``image_base64`` /
  ``image_url`` act as the *primary* frame (frame 0); extra frames carry
  wrist views, overhead views, or short clips for temporal tasks.
* ``depth_base64`` — optional 16-bit PNG depth map aligned to the
  primary frame. Lets a runner promote 2D detections into 3D without
  needing a separate reconstruction pass.
* ``camera_intrinsics`` / ``camera_pose`` — pinhole intrinsics and world
  pose of the primary camera, required for any structured action that
  emits metric 3D output (``detect_objects_3d``, ``predict_grasps``).
* ``history`` — ordered turns of prior context for agentic / stateful
  perception (e.g. "the mug from the previous turn is now on the tray").

Current cloud providers (Google / OpenAI / custom HTTP) ignore the
extended fields — they are preserved on the wire and on the run record
so edge runners (PyRoKi / ContactGraspNet / SAM3 wrappers) can pick them
up without a second protocol revision.
MLModelRunSchema.title: MLModelRunSchema
